title: `ward init` and project binding
description: Spec §7.1 and §11.2. Opaque project UUID in tracked .ward/project.json; binding to a canonical Git worktree root lives only in the encrypted vault. Unknown checkouts, copied IDs, nested repos, worktrees and moved paths never inherit a binding. Ward-managed CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block preserves every other block.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T10: unknown project, copied project ID, nested repo, worktree, moved path and unregistered clone cannot silently inherit a binding
T22: repeated init preserves user content and peer blocks; malformed markers and escaping symlinks are conflicts, not overwrites

implementationNotes: Design decisions recorded in docs/adr/0005-project-binding-identity.md (new ADR). Two points the spec leaves open, decided here and reported to the orchestrator: (1) a binding names the canonical worktree root AND that directory's device+inode (bigint, decimal strings), because a path alone cannot distinguish a fresh clone from the checkout it replaced at the same path, and spec §7.1 requires new clones to be handled explicitly; (2) registration is interactive only — a non-interactive caller is refused (denied/4, binding_requires_terminal) before the vault key is read, and there is deliberately no non-interactive register flag; --no-register prepares files without authority. Two non-interactive-asymmetries worth knowing: bare 'ward init' from a non-tty exits 4 even when the checkout happens to be registered already (Ward never reads the vault to answer a question it was not asked), and 'ward init' with no vault exits 3 (vault_not_found) after the scaffold is written, so a developer runs setup and re-runs init. P0 gap filed in the ADR: no unregister/rebind command exists, so a path bound to another project is resolved from the repository side (restore or remove the manifest).

REVIEW RETURNED (2026-09-28, after the handoff note; it supersedes step 1 of that note). Independent opum-workflow:reviewer pass over f56cc98, environment bun 1.3.14 / lore 0.11.0 / macOS APFS. VERDICTS: T10 not falsified - the only writer of a binding is behind the approved prompt plus the in-transaction re-check, and no shape found grants authority; T22 not falsified as worded (a refusing run leaves the marker file byte-identical, and no escaping link was ever written through). Verified rather than unbroken: cross-process vault concurrency 3 processes x 25 registrations all landed with no duplicate (root,device,inode) and no lost update; --no-register reaches neither vault nor keychain; escaping/dangling/directory-valued links, malformed manifest and schemaVersion 2 all refuse with bytes untouched; a repo that would contain the vault refuses. FIX LIST before merge, ranked: (F1 HIGH) init writes the manifest BEFORE the conflict decision (src/application/project.ts:190-202 vs the check at :218-256), so a BOUND checkout whose .ward/project.json was deleted gets a fresh unrelated id written, then exits 5 binding_conflict, and every later init conflicts again - wedged; the error hint says to restore the manifest, which is only actionable if the write had not happened (git restore works when it was committed, and not otherwise). Decide the conflict before any repository write, and give a bound directory a recovery path (write the vault's own id back into the manifest, or refuse with nothing written). (F2 MEDIUM) the documented agent+developer pairing - 'ward init --no-register --claude --codex' beside 'ward init' in a terminal - diverges the manifest from the binding in 8 of 12 synchronised rounds, which then trips F1's wedge; same ordering cause; the cheap part is re-reading the manifest after registering and refusing or reporting when it changed under the run. (F3 MEDIUM) an escaping symlink is followed on READ: resolve() checks containment only when the FINAL component is a link (src/adapters/project-files.ts:64-86) while lstatSync follows intermediate ones, so a checkout with .ward symlinked outside reads project.json from outside it (exit 0, manifest present) - no write escapes the root; fix in resolve(), which also closes F5 (containment rests on a single-level parent check). (F4 MEDIUM-LOW) bridges are written one at a time, so a conflict on a later target leaves earlier writes in place while the error says 'Ward did not change the file' and ADR 0005 says a conflict 'changes nothing'; pre-flight every target before writing any. (F7 INFO) the vault-directory guard is one-directional - a repository rooted inside ~/.ward is not refused. (F6 COSMETIC) the help layout defect is already fixed in aa45eef. ADR 0005 must be corrected with F3 and F4, whose sentences it falsifies. FORWARD RISK when WCLI-8 lands: bindingFor returns the binding for the directory regardless of what the manifest's project id says, and nothing outside initProject compares the two - a later consumer reading profiles from the manifest while using the binding's project would mix two projects. NOT CHECKED by the review: the successful registration path in the packaged binary (needs the real Keychain, which was forbidden), a real TTY registration, Linux/Windows, and any claim resting on a changed vault formatVersion.
